content.text:
**Finding submitted: deviation (LD), preferred-level cure.**

- **Responsive clause:** § 7.6 (p0032) is the only Customer-payable liquidated damages provision in the document — USD 25,000 per day, uncapped, for "any delay in providing a dependency." Searches for "liquidated", "penalt", early-termination/minimum fees, and "dependency" returned no other Customer-payable liquidated amount; § 27.3's "without penalty" and § 20.1's "penalties" run in our favour or against Vendor, and § 21.2 is a mutual consequentials exclusion (not flagged).
- **Why it fails fallback:** the fallback permits only an early-termination fee capped at three months' fees as the sole liquidated amount. A per-day accrual triggered by any (including trivial) delay, with no ceiling, is unbounded and can exceed remaining contract value — walk-away territory.
- **Cure:** surgical replacement of the offending words only, leaving "7.6 Customer shall pay … ." intact: Customer "pay[s] no liquidated damages or penalties under this Agreement." No clause cross-references § 7.6, so no retained formula or payment mechanic contemplates such a payment, and Vendor keeps its ordinary remedies for genuine delay.
